prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1119; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed first notice of loss. Insured reports a collision at an intersection while making a left turn. Other vehicle was approaching from the opposite direction. Insured states the oncoming vehicle was not visible until the impact. Police report requested.

Entry 2: Spoke with the insured by phone. Insured confirms no prior claims on this vehicle in the past several years. Photos of both vehicles received and added to the file. Damage appears consistent with a front-to-side impact on the insured's passenger side.

Entry 3: Claimant has retained counsel. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and logged. Bodily injury claim noted: claimant reports neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash. Medical authorization requested through counsel.

Entry 4: Received police report. Responding officer documented the insured's vehicle as turning left across the path of the other vehicle. Citation issued to the insured's driver for failure to yield. Witness statement from a pedestrian at the corner is pending.

Entry 5: Counsel's office sent medical records summary for the claimant's initial evaluation and follow-up treatment. Records reflect a diagnosis of whiplash-type cervical strain. Treatment plan is ongoing. Liability appears probable given the citation and physical evidence. Reserve review scheduled and file forwarded to the bodily injury unit.
